Pre-deploy review

Meridian Interface, screen by screen

Every view captured from a production build, the booking flow driven end to end, and the codebase audited for secrets, injection, accessibility and error handling. Four issues found and fixed; one left open for your call.

4 fixed 8 passed 1 open

Findings

  • Fixed

    Bookings did not appear in the client portal

    The portal read storage only when it first mounted. The most natural path — open “My Appointments”, tap “Book New Appointment”, book — left the list stale, so a client saw their booking missing and would reasonably assume it failed. It now refreshes on booking. Verified end to end: the list goes 2 → 3.

  • Fixed

    Personal data written to the browser console

    Every booking logged the full appointment — name, email, phone — to the console. Removed.

  • Fixed

    A staff-only portal advertised in public

    The footer showed “Studio login” in production even when no passcode was configured, pointing at a gate nobody could pass. It now appears only when the portal can actually be unlocked — which is why you will not find it in the screenshots below.

  • Fixed

    One network blip could lose a booking

    Submission tried once. A high-value booking now retries before falling back to the local copy.

  • Pass

    No secrets in the repository

    Scanned for keys, tokens and credentials: none committed. .gitignore covers .env and every variant.

  • Pass

    No injection surface

    No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no innerHTML assignment, no eval. React escapes all rendered values.

  • Pass

    No third-party scripts; fonts self-hosted

    Nothing executes from a CDN. Hanken Grotesk, Inter and the icon font are served from your own domain.

  • Pass

    Clean run across every screen

    Zero JavaScript errors and zero React warnings across all eight views, desktop and mobile.

  • Pass

    Mobile layout holds

    No horizontal scroll at 390px. Navigation correctly swaps to the bottom bar.

  • Pass

    Build is clean

    TypeScript reports no errors; production build succeeds at 45 modules, 94 kB gzipped.

  • Open

    Photography is hotlinked from Unsplash

    Twenty-four images load from images.unsplash.com. It works, but your visual identity then depends on a third party staying up and keeping those URLs. Worth self-hosting before you promote the site.

  • Pass

    TypeScript strict mode is on

    Enabled during hardening, and the project still typechecks with zero errors — a whole class of null and undefined bugs is now caught at build time rather than in front of a client.

  • Pass

    Booking form is labelled for screen readers

    Every field in the booking form and the quick-book modal carries an accessible label, so the form is usable with a screen reader.

Every screen

About the blank photography. These captures come from a sandbox with no outbound network, so the images hotlinked from Unsplash could not load. The hero renders because it is a local asset. On a real host every image appears — this is a limitation of the capture environment, not of your site.
